subtitle: Global Climate & Environmental Sentinel
brief_overview: Deploy a high-resolution remote-sensing observatory into Sun-Synchronous Low Earth Orbit (705 km altitude) to measure ecosystem health, forest carbon stocks, and urban heat islands.
objectives: Achieve stable 705 km Sun-synchronous circular orbit.
Perform global 16-day repeat multispectral imagery acquisition.
Maintain positive electrical energy balance during 35-minute orbital eclipse phases.
Downlink calibrated multispectral datasets to NASA ground receiving stations.
engineering_constraints: LEO Drag Compensation: Atmospheric drag requires attitude control and propulsion for orbit maintenance.
Orbital Eclipse: Satellite spends ~35 minutes of every 98-minute orbit in Earth's shadow; battery buffering is critical.
High Data Rate: Optical and SAR sensors generate heavy daily datasets requiring sufficient recorder capacity and downlink bandwidth.
educational_context: Earth observation satellites utilize Sun-synchronous orbits so they cross the equator at the same local solar time on every pass, providing consistent shadow angles and lighting for multi-year environmental comparisons. NASA's Earth Observing System (EOS) operates satellites like Terra, Aqua, and Landsat to monitor planetary changes.
